title: DDNYC WAS DDL TCG LAUNCH! Pack Rips to First Champion!
description: DDL TCG Community continues to HYPE the official LEGENDS TCG release!

body:
DDL TCG — DDNYC Combined Recap

 DDNYC is where Rise of the Pack left the screen and hit the table.

 The first rips

 Before the floor opened, Bark and Shibo cracked the first packs on a Bark subscriber Space out of DDNYC. Pack three ended on a holographic Gigatron . First Gigatron ever pulled. BradX called it the grail and a museum piece. That pull is the origin story of physical DDL.

The floor opens

 September 2, packs were everywhere. Official broadcast: Doginal Dogs went live welcoming the room. Box posted the scene straight: everyone ripping. Dro filmed a pack-opening clip. Swish posted the table. Rus caught Mac ripping and pulling a full-art Mento — Rus offered a free hotel room for the card. Devin said holding the cards in hand was the point. Poe lost it over Vee’s swag unbox and the TCG cards in the same drop. Quality talk stayed on stock, holos, and chase hits — not theory.

Chase sheet already public from the main account: Boogie, Helios, Toot, Mama Bark, Penny, Aria, Volt, Gigatron, Turbo, Darron, Atlas, Wiggles, Bender, Mento, Renza, Shiboshi, Shield, Hunter, Bark. The room spent two days proving those cards exist in foil, in sleeves, in people’s hands.

 Then they played

 September 3, first IRL DDL TCG tournament. Cards on felt. No screen.

 Dick won. Ammon second. Corn third. First prize included a Doginal Dog . Home reffed. Bomb hosted. Duck posted the podium.

 Finals were Dick vs Ammon. Roll called the match, then posted the result with video. Vee ran the X broadcasts. Guy streamed Kick. Kush ran the live bracket. And got 0–40’d by Dick in an opener and posted start-to-finish photos. Banter stayed in-pack: can’t hold Dick.

 @DDLTCG did not post through the weekend. Coverage was the floor.

 Three days, two facts: the packs are real, and Dick is the first IRL champion.

The timeline delivered another clear day of progress for Doginal Dogs Legends.

 New Card Reveal

 Bailey revealed Wiggles (V067) from the first edition set Rise of the Pack . The card quickly picked up strong engagement across the community and continues the steady daily reveal cadence. While not completely overpowering, the Wiggles Card is the HIGHEST draw for the Wizard creatures, with 7 mana required to play, dealing the enemy a 5 HP hit and requiring a 5HP hit to get destroyed. The power of the Wizard Deck aren’t in the individual cards themselves, but the Schema Spells that allow of many multiples on these attacks. More to come on how the Wizard Deck, and all the decks are shaping up in the Doginal Dogs LEGENDS TCG!

Competitive Play

 During the NFT Roundtable, Jag and DeFi went head-to-head. First game: Stock Neutral (Jag) vs Stock Wizard (DeFi) — DeFi took the win. Second game: Both switched to their custom decks — Jag took the win.

 Clean, public matches like this are exactly what the early competitive scene needs.

 Expect more public Spaces becomign trash talking sessions while members of the Doginal Dogs Community match up against one another and stream the gameplay live on X, Kick, and other platforms.

 Card Discussion

 On his Space The Great Reset , Bark went into specific card talk, including Wayne and which creatures are currently shaping up as one of the strongest for actual gameplay. These conversations are helping the community move past just collecting reveals and into real deck-building discussion. As the creator of the DDL TCG, his opinions and insights are always welcome for those interested in learning more about the game.

 Other Notes

 DeFi stayed active throughout the day, reacting to both the Wiggles reveal and broader community activity. The overall energy remains focused on the same things: new cards, public matches, and people actually playing the game.

 Wiggles is now public. Matches are being played and documented. Deck talk is getting more specific.

body:
DDL Update – August 14, 2026

 The timeline stayed active around Doginal Dogs Legends today.

 Card Reveal ‍ ‍

 Doginal Dogs CFO, Shield dropped the latest DDL card reveal, and this one was fitting: Shield . Another hand-drawn card from the Rise of the Pack set continues the daily reveal cadence the community has been running. The Shield card allows for 2 spells from the graveyard to your hand. It takes 5 mana to deal the card, 3 to get taken out, and gives 6 on the attack! This is a powerful card worth paying attention to. As we move forward, we will also connect these cards to the actual dogs they are modeled off of from the actual Doginal Dogs collection .

Tournament Momentum ‍ ‍

 Community member Home is organizing a bracketed DDL tournament. It will be live-streamed and framed as a pure deck-measuring contest. Interest is already being collected in the replies. This is one of the clearer signals that people are moving from theory into actual organized play.

title: How to Play Doginal Dogs Legends: Complete Rules Guide
description: Full rules for Doginal Dogs Legends (DDL): 40 HP heroes, 40-card decks, mana, combat, keywords, the DDL Coin, and all four game modes. Updated as rules are confirmed.
author: Box Meta
body:
DDL GAMEPLAY BETA IS ONLINE! VISIT DDLTCG.COM/PLAY TO TEST IT YOURSELF!

Doginal Dogs Legends is a lane-based competitive card game. Both heroes start at  40 health  with a  40-card deck , and you win by dropping the enemy hero to  0 . You spend  mana  to play creatures, spells, and traps, and attack with creatures that are  ready .

 Doginal Dogs has not published a standalone rulebook. Everything below is drawn from the official in-game How to Play reference and the Teach Pack tutorial at  ddltcg.com/play , plus beta play. Individual cards are not covered here — Rise of the Pack is still being revealed, and this page deals only with the rules that apply to all of them.

 How do you win?

 Reduce the enemy hero from 40 HP to 0. You control the bottom hero; your opponent is the top.

 That is the only win condition. There are powerful creatures and traps capable of wiping the entire board, but clearing the field doesn't itself win the game — hero health is untouched by it. Board control is a means, not the objective.

What happens on a turn?

 Every turn runs the same four steps:  mana up → draw → play and attack → end turn .

 Start.  You gain mana — turn 1 gives 1 crystal, increasing each turn  up to a maximum of 10 . You draw 1 card.

 Main.  Play creatures, spells, and traps by paying their cost. Attack with ready creatures.

 End.  Press End Turn and your opponent plays.

 Unspent mana does not carry over.  Every turn is a fresh budget, so holding back banks nothing.

 What is the DDL Coin?

 If you go  second , you get the Coin:  once per game you may play a card that costs 1 more than your current mana.

 That's a subtler compensation than the equivalent in other card games. It doesn't hand you a mana crystal or an extra card — it lets you cheat the curve exactly once, which makes the decision about  when  to spend it rather than whether. Holding it for the right turn is a real skill expression.

 How does the opening work?

 Each player draws an  opening hand of 4 cards , then one card per turn at the start of their turn.

 Hand maximum is 10.  Extra draws while your hand is full go straight to the graveyard, so overdrawing burns cards outright.

 What are the three card types?

 Creatures  occupy lanes, attack, and defend.  Spells  produce effects.  Traps  are set in advance and trigger in response.

 All three are played from hand during your Main phase by paying their cost.

 Spell and trap timing varies by card. Some resolve immediately and are spent — a spell that destroys a creature does its job and goes to the graveyard rather than staying on the board. Others persist, amplifying attacks or healing your hero over time.

 How is the board laid out?

 Each side has two rows of five.  L1–L5 hold creatures , and  S1–S5 hold spells and traps  — ten positions in total per player.

 Creatures placed in a lane stay there until they die. Spells and traps that resolve immediately don't occupy a slot once spent; only persistent cards remain in the S row.

 The Teach Pack never places anything in the S row, because the tutorial covers creature play only.

 How does combat work?

 - Tap a  ready  creature of yours — it glows.

- Tap a legal target: an enemy creature, or the enemy hero.

- Damage trades.

 Combat is  kill-gated : a creature dies when the damage it takes meets or exceeds its Health. Because damage goes both ways in an exchange, both creatures can die at once — the game calls this a  trade , where you destroy the enemy creature but lose yours doing it.

 A worked example: a creature with 4 Attack and 1 Health attacks a creature with 1 Attack and 2 Health. The attacker's 4 clears the defender's 2 Health, so the defender dies. The defender's 1 clears the attacker's 1 Health, so the attacker dies too. Both hit the graveyard.

 That threshold model rewards knowing exact numbers rather than tracking accumulated damage, and it turns high-attack, low-health creatures into deliberate one-for-one trades rather than lasting board presence.

 You can also  stack several attackers into one target  when legal, which is how you break through a defender no single creature can kill.

What is summoning sickness?

 A creature  cannot attack the turn it was played  — unless it has Rush, and even then it can only hit creatures, never the hero.

 A creature played on an earlier turn is  ready  and can attack anything legal, including the enemy hero.

 So a fresh creature is inert, a fresh Rush creature can trade, and a ready creature can do everything.

 What are the keywords?

 Seven appear in the official reference:  Taunt, Rush, Poison, Play, Death, Haunt,  and  Passive .

 Four apply generally:

 Taunt  — while it is on the board, it is the only legal target. Enemies cannot reach your hero or your other creatures first.

 Rush  — can attack enemy creatures the turn it is played, but never the enemy hero that turn.

 Play  — a one-time effect that fires when the card arrives from hand.

 Passive  — an ongoing effect that persists while the card is in play.

 Poison, Death,  and  Haunt  are tied to Zombie-class synergies rather than being universal mechanics, which is worth knowing if you're reading a card list and wondering why they don't appear everywhere.

 Note the distinction the game draws: the large text on a card is its name, while keywords are separate tags underneath. A card's name is not a rules term.

 How do classes work?

 Five are confirmed:  Wizard, Crown, Zombie, Bow,  and  Pirate .

 Decks do not have to commit to a single class.  You can mix freely, which makes deck building considerably more open than a hard class restriction would allow — the constraint is the three-copy limit and your mana curve, not your colour identity.

 Neutral  is not a fourth card type. It means a card isn't locked to a class, and a Neutral card is still a creature, spell, or trap. Heroes can be Neutral too.

 Some creatures go further and count as every class at once, which makes them unusually flexible when you're building around a class synergy.

 How many copies of a card can a deck hold?

 Three. On 40 cards that's a real constraint: maxing every slot would give roughly 13 distinct cards, so most decks run three-ofs for their core and fewer copies of situational answers.

What game modes are there?

 Teach Pack  — the guided lesson, recommended once.

 Vs Bot  — Easy or Advanced AI. Finishing matches earns  Miles , which accumulate with time played.

 BOOST  — both players start at 10 mana. Fast games built around high-cost cards.

 Vs Pack (PvP)  — Find Match for matchmaking, or Duel with a code for private games.  Live games are watchable , though duel-code games can only be joined with the code.

 The spectator function matters more than it first appears. It's the piece that makes organised competition and content creation possible, and it's already working in the beta.

 What is still undocumented

 - What happens when a deck runs out

- How Arena tiers progress

- Official tournament format and any banned or restricted list

 This page will be updated as each is confirmed.

title: Why Does DDL Rise of the Pack Have 111 Cards?
description: Rise of the Pack, the debut set for Doginal Dogs Legends, contains 111 cards. Doginal Dogs, the parent collection, launched on January 11, 2024 — written 1/11. The set size is almost certainly a reference to that date.  Doginal Dogs has not confirmed this publicly. What follows is an informed read,
author: Box Meta
body:
Rise of the Pack, the debut set for Doginal Dogs Legends, contains 111 cards. Doginal Dogs, the parent collection, launched on January 11, 2024 — written 1/11. The set size is almost certainly a reference to that date.

 Doginal Dogs has not confirmed this publicly. What follows is an informed read, not an official statement.

 Why 111 is an unusual number for a card set

 Trading card sets are typically sized around print-sheet math and product structure. Common set sizes cluster at round numbers or multiples that divide cleanly into packs and print runs — 100, 120, 150, 200. A set of 111 doesn't fall naturally out of that process. It's a number someone chose.

 That alone doesn't prove intent. But it does mean the number was decided rather than inherited from manufacturing constraints, which shifts the question from "why this size" to "why this specific figure."

What happened on January 11, 2024

 Alongside the official launch of Bitcoin ETFs on Wall Street, the Doginal Dogs launched as a free mint on January 11, 2024: 10,000 hand-curated pixel-art dogs inscribed on the Dogecoin blockchain. The dogs are inscriptions, created using technology similar to Bitcoin Ordinals, and are distinct from DRC-20, a separate fungible-token standard on Dogecoin.

 That date is the collection's origin point. Everything the brand has built since — the events, the merchandise line, the card game — traces back to it. 1/11 functions as the project's founding date in the same way a mint block does for other collections.

Why this reading is more than a coincidence

 Doginal Dogs has an established pattern of embedding references in its releases. Numbers, dates, and naming choices across the brand's drops tend to carry a second meaning for people who follow the project closely. Within the community, spotting them is part of how releases get received.

 Against that background, a 111-card set launching from a project founded on 1/11 is not a stretch. It's consistent with how this team works.

 The counterargument: 111 is also just an appealing number. Repdigits look good on packaging and read as premium. It's possible the date parallel is genuine and unintentional, or intentional and secondary to the aesthetics. Absent confirmation, this stays an inference.

 What would settle it

 A statement from the team in a Space, a reply, or the launch materials at DDNYC 2026 etc. would confirm or rule it out. Doginal Dogs hosts regular live sessions on X daily, where such meaning can be hinted at, or outright claimed.

 This page will be updated if that happens, with a note on where the confirmation came from.

 The short version

 111 cards, from a collection that launched 1/11. Not confirmed, but consistent with a team that builds these references in deliberately, and difficult to explain as coincidence given how set sizes are normally chosen.

title: Doginal Dogs Legends News & Card Info
description: Independent coverage of Doginal Dogs Legends (DDL), the hand-drawn trading card game from Doginal Dogs. Card details, set info, and launch news for Rise of the Pack.
author: Box Meta
body:
Doginal Dogs Legends (DDL) is a physical trading card game from Doginal Dogs, announced on August 6, 2026. Its debut set, Rise of the Pack, contains 111 hand-drawn cards and launches at DDNYC 2026 in New York City from September 2 to 4. Preorders opened at a discounted $170 per box and sold out in 32 hours. A digital version is already playable in beta at ddltcg.com/play .

 Doginal Dogs itself is a collection of 10,000 hand-curated pixel-art dogs inscribed on the Dogecoin blockchain, launched as a free mint in 2024. The dogs are inscriptions — created with technology similar to Bitcoin Ordinals — and are distinct from DRC-20, which is a separate fungible token standard on Dogecoin. Legends is the collection's move into physical product.

 This page collects every detail confirmed by Doginal Dogs so far, in one place. It will be updated as more is announced.

 How many cards are in Rise of the Pack?

 111 cards. Every one is original artwork drawn by hand by the Doginal Dogs team — not generated, not licensed. The set is distributed across rarity tiers, with rare and premium cards appearing less frequently in packs, a structure familiar to anyone who has opened Magic or Pokémon product.

 The number itself is probably deliberate: Doginal Dogs launched on January 11, 2024, and 111 is an unusual set size to arrive at by accident. More on why 111 almost certainly means 1/11.

 Doginal Dogs has not published a rarity breakdown, pull rates, or a tier-by-tier card count. Those numbers are the main open question for collectors, and this page will be updated if they are released.

 How do you actually play DDL?

 Players build a  40-card deck  and choose from distinct character classes. Decks combine three card types: creatures, spells, and traps.

 Deck-building is constrained by a copy limit:  no more than three of any single card . If you're running VOLT, you can include three copies at most. That cap is standard practice in competitive card games, and it's the rule that makes deck-building a real constraint rather than a matter of stacking the strongest card forty times.

 The company positions Legends as a competitive game first, describing mechanics intended to reward skill, deck-building, and long-term mastery while staying approachable for new players. Nearly two years of development went into it before announcement.

 Full rules have not been published. Until they are, the deck size, the class system, and the three card types are the only confirmed mechanical details.

When and where does DDL launch?

 Rise of the Pack debuts at  DDNYC 2026, September 2–4, 2026 , at Dream Downtown in Chelsea, Manhattan. Attendees will be among the first to play it in person as part of the event program.

 DDNYC 2026 sold out in under an hour when tickets went on sale. It runs alongside NFT.NYC, held September 1–3 in the same city, which makes the first week of September the densest gathering point of the year for this corner of the space.

 Preorders opened alongside the August 6 announcement and sold out in 32 hours.

 What's in a box, and what did it cost?

 A box contains  24 packs at 10 cards per pack — 240 cards total . Preorder pricing was  $170 per box , a discount off the eventual retail price.

 That works out to roughly  71 cents per card . For a 111-card set, a single box holds more than twice the set size in raw card count, which is generous by trading card game standards — though rarity distribution means completing the set from one box is a different question entirely, and pull rates haven't been published.

 Preorders sold out in 32 hours. Doginal Dogs' launch materials still describe preorders as open, but they closed on August 7.

 Is there a digital version?

 Yes, and it's already playable. A browser-based digital client is live at  ddltcg.com/play , where the Doginal Dogs community has accumulated tens of hours of games during the beta testing phase.

 This is the detail most coverage has missed. Doginal Dogs' launch materials describe a digital format "in development" with a beta waitlist, which reads as forthcoming — but the client is functional now and has been in active community testing ahead of the physical launch. The writer of this page has played close to 100 beta games.

 No public timeline has been given for a full digital release, and pricing has not been announced.

Why does a 111-card hand-drawn set matter?

 Two reasons worth separating.

 The first is production. Hand-drawing 111 cards over two years is an unusual commitment in a space where most collectible projects generate art programmatically. Co-founder Christian "Bark" Barker tied that choice directly to community expectations, noting that "every single card was drawn by hand."

 The second is track record. Doginal Dogs has produced more than 25 self-funded events across four continents since launching in January 2024, and says it has never cancelled an announced event. DDVegas at The Venetian in October 2025 sold out and peaked at 2,500 attendees, with secondary-market tickets trading above $700. DDNYC 2026 is produced with TAO Hospitality Group, whose venues include TAO, Marquee, Lavo, and Avenue.

 That history is the useful signal for anyone weighing a preorder on a first-edition set: this is a team that has shipped events at scale, repeatedly, on its own money.

 Can card shops stock DDL?

 Yes. Card shops and retailers anywhere in the world can apply to carry future print runs through  ddltcg.com/stores .

 Given that the first preorder wave sold out in 32 hours, retail distribution is the most likely route to product for anyone who missed it. No details have been published on wholesale pricing, minimum orders, or when approved stores would receive stock.

 What hasn't been made public

 Much of the set is already known within the Doginal Dogs community — the full catalogue has circulated internally, and card backs briefly appeared on the official site before being taken down. What follows is what Doginal Dogs has not confirmed publicly as of this writing:

 - Rarity tier counts by class, and the total number of giga rares

- Pack configuration and pull rates

- Print run size for the first edition

- The full class list and complete rules text

- How hybrid cards interact with class restrictions

- Full digital release timeline and pricing

- Retail pricing after the preorder window, and whether a second wave is planned

 This page will be updated as each is confirmed.

 Sources

 - Doginal Dogs Legends announcement, August 6, 2026

- DDNYC 2026 announcement, May 26, 2026

- Official site and card gallery: ddltcg.com
